name: Computer Networks
preamble: This course provides the learners a clear understanding of computer networks from local area networks to the global Internet. This course covers the physical aspects of computer networks, layers of OSI Reference model, and inter-networking. The course helps the learners to compare and analyze the existing network technologies and choose a suitable network design for a given system.
textbooks: J.F. Kurose and K.F. Ross, Computer networking: A top-down approach, 6th edition, Pearson, 2017
Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Computer Networks, 4/e, PHI (Prentice Hall India), 2003
Behrouz A Forouzan, Data Communication and Networking, 4/e, Tata McGraw Hill, 2007
referenceBooks: Larry L Peterson and Bruce S Dave, Computer Networks – A Systems Approach, 5/e, Morgan Kaufmann, 2011
Fred Halsall, Computer Networking and the Internet, 5/e, 2005
James F. Kurose, Keith W. Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 6/e, 2013
Keshav, An Engineering Approach to Computer Networks, Addison Wesley, 1998
W. Richard Stevens. TCP/IP Illustrated Volume 1, Addison-Wesley, 2005
William Stallings, Computer Networking with Internet Protocols, 6. William Prentice-Hall, 2004
Request for Comments (RFC) Pages IETF - https://www.ietf.org/rfc.html
E. Altman and T. Jimenez, NS2 Simulator for Beginners, 2003

modules.name: Introduction to Data Communication and Internet
syllabus: Introduction to Data Communication - Modes of communication, Physical topologies
Performance indicators - Bandwidth, Throughput, Latency, Queuing time, Bandwidth-Delay product
Basics of Internet, The Network Edge, The Network Core
Protocol layers and their service models: The OSI reference model

modules.name: Application Layer
syllabus: Principles of network applications, The Web and the HTTP
Electronic mail, Multipurpose Internet Mail Extension (MIME)
Video streaming and Content Distribution Networks

modules.name: Network Layer
syllabus: Routing Algorithms – Link state and Distance Vector Routing
Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) and Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP)
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP), Reverse Address Resolution Protocol (RARP)
Bootstrap Protocol (BOOTP) and Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP)

modules.name: Data link layer
syllabus: Medium Access Control (MAC) sublayer – Channel allocation problem, Multiple access protocols
Wireless LANs - 802.11, Repeaters, Hubs, Bridges, Switches, Routers and Gateways
